newsitem.title: INDIA: Singh sees investors losing confidence in India.
newsitem.headline: Singh sees investors losing confidence in India.

text.p: India's United Front government has fallen short of its economic targets and failed to gain the confidence of investors, former Finance Minister Manmohan Singh told the Economic Times newspaper on Monday.
Singh -- the architect of bold economic reforms begun in 1991 -- said in an interview even the ruling government admitted economic reforms were not on track.
"The political reality is that we have a hotch-potch coalition which has not even been able to implement what it agreed in its common minimum programme," Singh was quoted as saying.
India's ruling coalition led by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda released its economic targets last year.
Singh said the government had "broadly continued" the reforms initiated by the Congress Party "but in a manner which does not generate enough confidence."
He cited Suzuki Motor Corp which has not been allowed to increase its 50 percent stake in car maker Maruti Udyog Ltd. The government holds the rest of Maruti's equity.
"Suzuki is the most successful Japanese investment here. Now, if you want to attract investment from Japan, and you don't handle that case well, it will send wrong signals," Singh said.
He said the targeted seven percent growth rate would not be possible if investments and exports were weak and infrastructure was not improved.
Singh said India was following a "disastrous policy" by financing current consumption through borrowings.
"I believe that if you have an unsustainable deficit in any major commodity, whether it is power or energy, you cannot finance current consumption by borrowing," he said.
He said India should move towards deregulation of oil products at a "measured pace" over two to three years.
